v1_problem: Billing dispute tickets at Lakeside Water Utility doubled from ~600/month to ~1,200-1,260/month between July and August-September 2026 (E-07) because manual meter-reading route completion fell to 88% against a 95% target over that window, covering 9,200 manual-read accounts (E-02); the resulting missed field reads trigger estimate substitution in the billing import step, and this substitution channel accounts for the 41% of disputed bills that were on ESTIMATED reads (E-04), producing inaccurate bills that drive a material share of the dispute surge. Response-handling speed is not the mechanism, since dispute response times remain within SLA throughout the surge (E-01).
v2_problem: Billing dispute tickets at Lakeside Water Utility roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1,180-1,260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-07). For the ESTIMATED-read disputed-bill cohort (1,240 of 3,025 disputed bills, 41%, E-04), 95.5% (1,184/1,240) had an AMI read delivered before cutoff but were rejected at billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-12). This is driven by validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 at the surge's onset, which compares raw AMI register values to 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling (E-13), against firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) whose register unit is 0.1 m3 instead of whole m3 (E-14) — causing normal consumption to be misflagged as a high-consumption spike and rejected, forcing estimate substitution and producing bills customers dispute. Field route/staffing shortfalls and AMI delivery degradation are not the mechanism for this cohort, since reads were delivered before cutoff but rejected at import (E-12); the cause of the remaining 59% ACTUAL-read disputed cohort is not yet established.
